source: MemRL: Self-Evolving Agents via Runtime Reinforcement Learning on Episodic Memory
summary: Non-parametric RL applied to episodic memory lets agents incrementally update what they remember about past strategies across runs without fine-tuning. Benchmarks on BigCodeBench and ALFWorld show it significantly outperforms passive semantic matching.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly addresses Limitation #8 (no agent memory across runs); architecture is layerable atop existing agentSkillRepository pattern

summary: Introduces Progressive Interval Estimation (PIE): agents predict upper/lower bounds on remaining budget at each planning step. Key finding: frontier models are consistently over-optimistic, detecting failure only in the final 20% of budget.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly addresses Limitation #6 (no test-time compute scaling) and the fixed EXECUTOR_TIMEOUT_MS that causes unnecessary AIBlocked transitions on complex tasks

source: A Self-Healing Framework for Reliable LLM-Based Autonomous Agents
summary: Monitor-detect-diagnose-recover-verify loop where different failure types trigger targeted recovery: timeouts→retry with backoff, stale retrieval→evidence refresh, malformed args→repair. Generates verbal self-critique stored in memory for conditioned retry.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — maps 1:1 to AgentForge failure modes; eliminates hard reset to Todo on failure (Limitation #3, #5)

source: Self-Healing Agentic Orchestrators for Reliable Tool-Augmented LLM Systems
summary: Companion paper to arXiv 2605.06737 providing extended taxonomy of orchestrator failure modes and recovery patterns with empirical results.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — corroborates and extends the self-healing framework with additional failure taxonomies applicable to AgentForge's stage machine

source: Letta Code: A Memory-First Coding Agent (MemGPT evolution)
summary: Three-tier OS-inspired memory (Core/Archival/Recall) where the agent decides when to page information in/out through function calls. Reached #1 open-source on Terminal-Bench at 42.5% on hardest CLI tasks (March 2026).
relevanceToAgentForge: High — production-validated memory architecture directly applicable to wrapping Claude Code invocations; corroborates HID-170 trajectory memory approach

source: PASTE: Act While Thinking — Pattern-Aware Speculative Tool Execution
summary: Exploits recurring tool-call patterns in agent workflows to pre-execute likely future calls while the LLM generates. Achieves 48.5% reduction in task completion time and 1.8x tool throughput. Deployed as a sidecar alongside existing runtimes.
relevanceToAgentForge: High on novelty/impact but Low on immediate feasibility — AgentForge's sequential ProcessRunner would require significant restructuring; no parallel process management infrastructure today

source: B-PASTE: Beam-Aware Pattern-Guided Speculative Execution for Resource-Constrained LLM Agents
summary: Extends PASTE to maintain a bounded beam of future execution subgraphs ranked by expected critical-path reduction; designed for resource-constrained environments.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — builds on PASTE; interesting follow-up but requires PASTE infrastructure first

source: Speculative Actions: A Lossless Framework for Faster Agentic Systems
summary: Uses a fast/cheap model to predict likely future tool calls and execute in parallel before the primary LLM commits. Predictions match ~55% of the time; mismatches discard the result. Lossless by design.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — strong guarantees but sequential architecture makes parallel branch execution a significant lift; deferred until PASTE pattern is evaluated

source: ProRL Agent: Rollout-as-a-Service for RL Training of Multi-Turn LLM Agents (NVIDIA NeMo Gym)
summary: Decouples agentic rollout orchestration from RL training via a standalone HTTP service with async three-stage assembly line. Validated on software engineering, math, STEM, and coding tasks.
relevanceToAgentForge: High potential but Medium feasibility — requires RL training infrastructure not present in AgentForge; better suited as a future phase once telemetry data is collected

source: Maestro: RL to Orchestrate Hierarchical Model-Skill Ensembles
summary: Trains a lightweight 4B policy to dynamically compose ensembles of frozen expert models and a two-tier skill library. Surpasses GPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Pro on 10 multimodal benchmarks with only a 4B orchestrator.
relevanceToAgentForge: High impact but requires policy training infrastructure; better addressed once AgentForge accumulates per-stage performance data (a dependency)

source: Uno-Orchestra: Parsimonious Agent Routing via Selective Delegation
summary: Learns a unified orchestration policy that selectively decomposes tasks and dispatches subtasks to model-primitive pairs via RL. Achieves 77.0% macro pass@1 at lower per-query cost by routing simple subtasks to cheap models.
relevanceToAgentForge: High strategic relevance but requires RL training data to learn routing policy — blocked by lack of historical performance data

source: Reinforcement Learning for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems through Orchestration Traces
summary: Formalizes orchestration as five sub-decisions (when to spawn, whom to delegate, how to communicate, aggregate, and stop). Proposes training on orchestration trace logs as supervised signal for learning coordination policies.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — AgentForge's existing event logs are exactly the orchestration traces described; deferred as implementation requires RL training infrastructure

source: MIRROR: Converging Cognitive Principles as Computational Mechanisms for AI Reasoning
summary: Dual-process reasoning (fast/System-1 and slow/System-2 modes) with dynamic switching based on task confidence signals. Detects local optima loops in naive reflection and escalates to different reasoning mode.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — escalation pattern (detect stuck remediation loop, escalate to different model) is valuable for Limitation #7; deferred as it overlaps with HID-168 scope

source: Google A2A Protocol v0.3 / Agent Communication Protocol (ACP)
summary: A2A (donated to Linux Foundation) and ACP (IBM/BeeAI) are now dominant standards for agent-to-agent communication. A2A v0.3 adds gRPC, security card signing, and streaming via SSE. Manages full task lifecycle: Discovery→Authorization→Communication.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — enabling parallel agent execution (Limitation #2) would require A2A-style communication; but AgentForge's CLI subprocess model makes this a larger architectural change

source: LlamaIndex Workflows 1.0: Lightweight Async Agent Orchestration
summary: Standalone event-driven async-first step-based execution model. Steps emit and consume typed events; runtime handles fan-out/fan-in, parallel branches, and cancellation natively. No external state store required.
relevanceToAgentForge: High potential but too early — adopting Workflows 1.0 as the execution backbone would require significant architectural refactor of the state machine; watch for maturity

source: LangGraph Checkpointing and Failure Recovery Patterns (2026 production maturity)
summary: LangGraph's checkpointing system serializes full graph state after each node to PostgreSQL or Redis — enabling resume-after-crash, rollback, and branching into parallel timelines. Over 70% of production agent deployments now use graph structures with human-in-the-loop.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge's state machine already conceptually resembles LangGraph; adopting LangGraph TS SDK would be a significant dependency addition

source: Cost-Aware Speculative Execution for LLM-Agent Workflows (Five-Dimension Method)
summary: Frames speculative execution as a five-dimensional cost-aware decision problem: latency, token cost, quality, reliability, and parallelism potential. Provides unified scoring to decide when speculation is worth overhead; proposes dynamic model cascades.
relevanceToAgentForge: High on novelty but depends on PASTE/speculative infrastructure; deferred until parallel execution capability exists

source: AgentPRM: Process Reward Models for LLM Agents via Step-Wise Promise and Progress
summary: Re-defined PRM capturing both interdependence between sequential decisions and contribution to final goal. Monte Carlo rollouts compute reward targets; 3B models trained with AgentPRM outperform GPT-4o and are 8x more compute-efficient.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — step-wise evaluation is valuable for scoring plan steps; deferred as it requires training a PRM or integrating an existing one

source: Yohei Nakajima: Better Ways to Build Self-Improving AI Agents
summary: Synthesizes design patterns, pros/cons, and practical lessons for self-improving agents including Gödel Agent (self-referential architecture that proposes and accepts self-modifications if they pass improvement tests). Published Dec 2025.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low-Medium — conceptual overview useful for framing but no new implementation pattern beyond what arXiv papers provide
